title: Get Data: Sources, Storage Modes and Parameters

toc.title: Connect to data sources and shared semantic models
Data source settings, credentials and privacy levels
Choose between Direct Lake, DirectQuery and Import

html:
1Connect to data sources and shared semantic models

On the Home tab of Power BI Desktop, Get data opens the list of Power Query connectors: files such as Excel, CSV, JSON and XML, databases, online services, cloud sources and the web. Pick a connector, sign in, then choose Load or Transform Data.

Button What happens
Load The data goes straight into the model
Transform Data The Power Query Editor opens so you can clean and shape first

Some connectors also ask for a storage mode: Import or DirectQuery. Section 3 explains how to choose.

To reuse work that someone else already published, use a shared semantic model. On the Home tab choose Get data, then Power BI semantic models, and pick the model. You build new reports on the existing model instead of copying the data. The measures and relationships stay in one place, so every report shows the same numbers.

Need Choice
Same measures and no extra copy of the data Connect to the shared semantic model
Your own shaping of a source Connect to the source with a Power Query connector

You need Build permission on the model to create new content from it (module 15). A source on a private network or on-premises needs a gateway for refresh in the service (module 14). Cloud sources do not.

Exam tip

. To build a new report on an existing semantic model without copying data, use Get data, then Power BI semantic models. It needs Build permission on the model.

2Data source settings, credentials and privacy levels

In the Power Query Editor choose Data source settings on the Home tab. In Desktop you find it under Transform data on the Home tab. The dialog lists the sources in the current file and the global permissions saved on your computer.

Button Use it to
Edit Permissions Change the credentials and the privacy level
Clear Permissions Remove saved credentials so Power BI asks again
Change Source Point the query at another server, database or file path

The credential type must match the source, such as Windows, Basic (user name and password), Organizational account or Anonymous. After you publish, the refresh credentials live in the semantic model settings in the service. Only the model owner can edit them. Another user must take over the model first.

Privacy levels stop Power Query from sending data from one source to another by accident when it combines sources. Each source has its own level.

Level Meaning
None No level is set yet
Private Sensitive: its data is never sent to any other source
Organizational Its data can go to Private and Organizational sources, not Public ones
Public Its data can go to any source

When a query would break these rules, Power Query blocks the combination and shows an error about privacy levels. The option to ignore privacy levels is off by default and does not apply to published models.

Exam tip

. Private data is never sent to another source, and Public data can go to any source. Organizational sits between them: it can go to Private and Organizational sources, not Public.

Exam tip

. Credentials and privacy levels are set in Data source settings, with Edit Permissions. In the service, only the model owner edits the credentials.

3Choose between Direct Lake, DirectQuery and Import

The storage mode decides where the data lives and when it is current. Import and DirectQuery work with any license.

Import DirectQuery Direct Lake
Data Copied into the in-memory model Stays in the source Delta tables in OneLake, read by the VertiPaq engine
Current when After a refresh Every visual queries the source A refresh copies only metadata (framing), in seconds
Refresh Pro: up to 8 a day; PPU, Premium, Fabric: up to 48 Dashboard tiles refresh hourly by default No gateway can refresh it
Limits Data must fit the model A query over 1,000,000 rows fails; service timeout 4 minutes; 10 connections per source by default Needs a Fabric capacity (F SKU); not in My workspace
Also Fully interactive visuals Needs query folding; no automatic date hierarchy, so build a date table No hybrid tables, partitions or user-defined aggregations

Choose DirectQuery when the data changes too often, is too large to import, the source security must be kept (single sign-on), data-sovereignty rules limit copies, or the source has server-defined measures. Choose Direct Lake when the data is already Delta tables in OneLake and you want Import-like speed without scheduled copies. Choose Import when none of those apply.

Direct Lake on OneLake does not fall back to DirectQuery. Direct Lake on SQL endpoints can fall back to DirectQuery, for example for SQL views, granular SQL security or when guardrails are exceeded. The model property is Direct Lake behavior.

Other options mix modes. Hybrid tables combine Import and DirectQuery partitions. Dual storage suits shared dimensions. Aggregation tables and automatic aggregations speed up DirectQuery.

Exam tip

. Import: Pro allows up to 8 scheduled refreshes a day, and PPU, Premium and Fabric allow up to 48. Direct Lake refresh copies only metadata.

Exam tip

. DirectQuery: a query returning more than 1,000,000 rows fails, the service timeout is 4 minutes and the default is 10 connections per source. Direct Lake needs a Fabric capacity, and no gateway can refresh it.

4Create and modify parameters

A parameter stores a value that queries can use, so you change the value once instead of editing many queries. Create one on the Home tab with Manage Parameters, then New Parameter. You can also right-click a query that holds a constant and choose Convert to Parameter.

Property Meaning
Name How steps refer to the parameter
Description Help text for the person who changes it
Required Whether a value must be given
Type Any, Text, Decimal Number, Date and so on
Suggested Values Any value, List of values or Query
Default Value The value used when none is chosen
Current Value The value the queries use now

A parameter does nothing until a step uses it. Edit the step, for example Filter Rows or the Source step, and pick the parameter instead of a typed value. On the View tab choose Parameters, then Always allow, so that the dialogs offer your parameters.

Parameters let you switch the source, server, database, file path or filter values. They also drive DirectQuery dynamic M parameters. To modify a parameter, open Manage Parameters and edit its properties or its current value. After publishing, the model owner can change values in the semantic model settings in the service.

let
    Source = Sql.Database(ServerName, DatabaseName),
    Sales = Source{[Schema = "dbo", Item = "Sales"]}[Data],
    Recent = Table.SelectRows(Sales, each [OrderDate] >= StartDate)
in
    Recent
Exam tip

. Switch between a test and a production server with a parameter used in the Source step. Convert to Parameter turns a constant query into a parameter.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A finance team published a semantic model with approved measures. An analyst needs a new report that uses the same measures and must not copy the data. What should the analyst do?

  • AImport the model's source tables again into a new file
  • BExport the model's tables to Excel and load that workbook
  • CUse Get data and the Power BI semantic models option
  • DCreate a new model and rewrite the measures in DAX
Show the answer

Answer: C. Connecting to the shared semantic model reuses its measures and relationships without a second copy of the data.

S2An analyst changed a SQL database password, and Power BI Desktop now asks for credentials. Where can the saved credentials be updated?

  • AIn Data source settings, with Edit Permissions
  • BIn Manage Parameters, by editing the current value
  • CIn Model view, by editing the column properties
  • DIn Query Settings, by renaming the Source step
Show the answer

Answer: A. Saved credentials and privacy levels are changed in Data source settings with Edit Permissions.

S3A query combines a salary table with a public web table. The salary data must never be sent to any other source. Which setting should the salary source have?

  • APublic, so its data can go to any source
  • BOrganizational, so Public sources are blocked
  • CIgnore levels, so the checks are turned off
  • DPrivate, so its data goes to no other source
Show the answer

Answer: D. Only the Private level stops a source's data from being sent to any other source.

S4A retailer keeps sales as Delta tables in OneLake on a Fabric F SKU capacity. Analysts want Import-like speed without scheduled copies of the data. Which storage mode fits?

  • AImport mode with an hourly scheduled refresh
  • BDirect Lake mode on the OneLake Delta tables
  • CDirectQuery mode with a hybrid history table
  • DDual mode on the large sales fact table
Show the answer

Answer: B. Direct Lake reads the Delta tables in OneLake with the VertiPaq engine, so nothing is copied on a schedule.

S5A team must switch the same report between a test server and a production server without editing each query. What should the analyst create?

  • AA calculated column that stores the server name per row
  • BA measure that returns the server name in a card visual
  • CA parameter for the server, used in the Source step
  • DA slicer in which viewers type the name of the server
Show the answer

Answer: C. A parameter used in the Source step lets you change the server in one place.

S6A large model moves from Import to Direct Lake. What does a refresh of the Direct Lake model now do?

  • AIt copies only metadata, which takes seconds
  • BIt reloads every Delta table into memory
  • CIt runs through an on-premises gateway
  • DIt sends a query to the source for each visual
Show the answer

Answer: A. A Direct Lake refresh copies only metadata (framing), so it completes in seconds.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What are the four privacy levels?

Show the answer

None, Private, Organizational and Public.

R2What happens to a DirectQuery query that returns more than 1,000,000 rows?

Show the answer

It fails.

R3Where do you edit saved credentials in Desktop?

Show the answer

Data source settings, with Edit Permissions.

R4How many scheduled refreshes a day does Pro allow, and how many do PPU, Premium and Fabric allow?

Show the answer

Up to 8 on Pro, and up to 48 on PPU, Premium and Fabric.

R5What does Direct Lake read?

Show the answer

Delta tables in OneLake, on a Fabric capacity.

R6How do you create a parameter?

Show the answer

Home, then Manage Parameters, then New Parameter, or Convert to Parameter on a constant query.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Shared model Get data, Power BI semantic models: reuse measures, no copy; needs Build permission
Data source settings Edit Permissions (credentials, privacy level), Clear Permissions, Change Source; only the owner edits credentials in the service
Privacy levels None; Private never sent; Organizational not to Public; Public to any source
Import data copied into the model; Pro 8 refreshes a day, PPU, Premium and Fabric 48
DirectQuery data stays in the source; over 1,000,000 rows fails; 4-minute timeout; 10 connections by default
Direct Lake Delta tables in OneLake; Fabric F SKU; no gateway; refresh copies metadata; OneLake variant has no fallback
Parameters Manage Parameters or Convert to Parameter; Type, Suggested Values, Current Value; use in a step
